rulings: CENSUS METHOD (read-only, prod, 2026-09-26/27): paginated {maxItemCount:500, maxDegreeOfParallelism:-1} scans of card_catalog under hiq:baseball:2026:bowman:, hiq:baseball:2026:bowman-mega: and hiq:baseball:2026:bowman-chrome-mega-box:, no cross-partition COUNT/GROUP BY. Paired candidates by (cardNumber, printRun, isAuto) -- a LOOSE key, because the STRICT key (cardNumber, parallelSlug, printRun, isAuto) found ZERO matches across all three setKeys: `bowman`'s Mega-Chrome-rung parallel text ('Mega Chrome Mojo Refractor', 'Mega Chrome <Color> Mojo Refractor') never matches `bowman-chrome-mega-box`'s own spelling ('Base Mega Mojo Refractor', 'Base Mega Image Variations') at the slug level, by product design (R75's whole point: the two lines spell the same rung DIFFERENTLY).

MEASURED: bowman has 64,987 total 2026 card_catalog rows (2,858 carry "mega" in parallel text or id parallel-slug). bowman-mega has 7,235 total rows, ZERO of which carry "mega" in parallel text or id parallel-slug -- its own rows are plain checklist numbering (BCP-###, BMA-##, BST-##, plain numbers) with parallel text like 'Navy Mojo Refractor', 'Green Mojo Refractor', never repeating the word 'mega' (the word lives in the setKey segment, not the rung). bowman-chrome-mega-box has 1,126 total rows, 264 of which carry 'mega' in parallel text.

THE LOOSE PAIRING (75 candidates, cardNumber+printRun+isAuto only, ignoring parallel spelling) found NO bowman<->bowman-mega pairs at all -- every one of the 75 pairs a `bowman` Mega-Chrome-rung row shares a (cardNumber, printRun, isAuto) key with is a `bowman-chrome-mega-box` row, never a `bowman-mega` row. Of those 75, 71 are DIFFERENT players (namesAgree=false) -- e.g. hiq:baseball:2026:bowman:78:mega-chrome-mojo-refractor:no-auto (Cole Young) vs hiq:baseball:2026:bowman-chrome-mega-box:78:base-mega-mojo-refractor:no-auto (Bryce Eldridge) -- the DOCUMENTED, CORRECT cross-product numbering coincidence R75's own code comment names explicitly (#52 Ohtani on plain Mega Box vs #52 JJ Wetherholt on Chrome Mega Box). These are NOT duplicates: they are two different real cards that happen to share a card number across two genuinely distinct 2026 products, exactly as R75 rules. Retiring either side would delete a real, checklist-backed card.

ONLY 4 of the 75 pairs namesAgree=true, and all 4 are bowman<->bowman-chrome-mega-box, not bowman<->bowman-mega: Francisco Lindor #17 (hiq:baseball:2026:bowman:17:mega-chrome-mojo:no-auto / hiq:baseball:2026:bowman:17:mega-chrome-mojo-refractor:no-auto, both checklist-grade, vs hiq:baseball:2026:bowman-chrome-mega-box:17:base-mega-mojo-refractor:no-auto) and the CRA- Mega Autographs pair for Bryce Eldridge and Roman Anthony (hiq:baseball:2026:bowman:cra-be/cra-ra:mega-autographs-image-variations:auto vs hiq:baseball:2026:bowman-chrome-mega-box:cra-be/cra-ra:rookies-mega-autographs:auto). ALL FOUR carry ZERO sales at either address (salesTotal=0 on both sides, by the dual sales-at-id check). No sale needs repointing for any of these four, and no catalog row is unsupported by a checklist on either side -- both are checklist-grade (source checklistcenter / checklistcenter-2026-08-29), so R75's own doctrine (a derived row never outvotes a checklist row) does not apply to a checklist-vs-checklist pair: this is the SAME PHYSICAL PRINT filed twice under two different product families' checklists, which is a product-family boundary question (is a Lindor Mega Chrome Mojo the SAME print as bowman-chrome-mega-box's Base Mega Mojo Refractor, or a genuinely separate insert?) rather than a spelling-collapse this lane is licensed to answer -- flagged 'needs ruling' in the PR body, not resolved here.

THE STATED EXAMPLE (hiq:baseball:2026:bowman:52:mega-chrome-mojo:no-auto and 'its bowman-mega twin') DOES NOT EXIST AS WRITTEN: point-read and cross-partition query both confirm hiq:baseball:2026:bowman-mega:52:mega-chrome-mojo:no-auto has NEVER existed in card_catalog, and #52 under bowman-chrome-mega-box is JJ Wetherholt (base-mega-image-variations / base-mega-mojo-refractor / base-mega-image-variations-autograph), not Ohtani -- the two #52s are the documented different-card coincidence, not a duplicate pair.

WHAT THE 155-ROW REFUSAL ACTUALLY IS. repoint-sales-to-sibling-product.cjs's MODE=by-player (added 2026-09-26, this same day) is a SALES discovery lane, not a card_catalog census: it scans stored sold_comps rows whose EXACT hobbyiqCardId/cardId has NO checklist-grade catalog row, checks whether the FROM product's checklist row at that number names a DIFFERENT player (namesAgree=false), and then asks whether EXACTLY ONE sibling of the FROM product's registered family (productParentOf-derived, e.g. bowman-chrome's siblings: bowman-chrome-mega-box, bowman-chrome-prospects, bowman-chrome-nscc, bowman-chrome-draft, bowman-chrome-draft-picks-and-prospects -- bowman-chrome-sapphire excluded as a never-crossing specialization) has a checklist row at that number agreeing with the sale's player. 'ambiguous-sibling' fires when TWO OR MORE siblings agree -- the sale's number and player are both real, but more than one sibling product could be the true home, so the lane refuses rather than guess. The script's own worked example in its docblock (added today) is titles=bowman-chrome, scope=baseball:2026 -- FROM=bowman-chrome, not bowman -- which matches this census's own finding that the ONLY same-number collisions bowman's Mega-Chrome rungs have are against bowman-chrome-mega-box, never bowman-mega directly.

THEREFORE: there is no catalog-row duplication to retire under R75 for (bowman, bowman-mega) as stated. bowman-mega is a real, distinct, checklist-populated product (7,235 rows) that simply does not share ANY (cardNumber, parallel-rung) address with bowman's Mega-Chrome rungs -- the two never collide because bowman-mega's own rows use plain/BCP-/BMA-/BST- numbering with its OWN parallel vocabulary, disjoint from bowman's 'Mega Chrome Mojo' text. The collision R75 exists to resolve is bowman's Mega-Chrome-rung PARALLEL TEXT (a rung that historically got filed under flagship bowman because pre-R75 ingests, dated 2026-08-29 -- three weeks before R75's 2026-09-19 ruling -- had no year-aware router) landing at the SAME NUMBER as bowman-chrome-mega-box's own base-mega rungs, which is a routing/sales-repoint question the by-player lane already exists to answer, and a checklist-vs-checklist product-boundary question for the 4 namesAgree=true pairs above, which needs Drew's ruling.

SOURCE-PREDATES-RULING CHECK (asked in the task): bowman's Mega-Chrome-rung rows are overwhelmingly source=checklistcenter-2026-08-29 (dated 2026-08-29), which is BEFORE R75 (Drew, 2026-09-19). catalogAuthorityOf classifies checklistcenter-2026-08-29 as checklist (matches /^(checklistcenter|checklist|checklistinsider|beckett)/). So yes: these are pre-ruling checklist ingests, landed under generic bowman before the year-aware bowman/bowman-mega/bowman-chrome-mega-box router (hobbyIqCardId.service.ts, BOWMAN_MEGA_BOX_SPLIT_FROM_YEAR gate) existed to route them correctly. Nothing has gone back and re-keyed these already-ingested checklist rows onto the router's post-R75 answer -- but since the router answer for a BARE 'Bowman Mega Box' (no Chrome) title is bowman-mega, and bowman's OWN rows are all Mega CHROME rungs (title says Chrome), the router would in fact leave them at bowman-chrome-mega-box's family, not bowman-mega, for any of them that actually belong on the Chrome side -- reinforcing that this is a bowman<->bowman-chrome-mega-box question, not a bowman<->bowman-mega one.
